study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities unveil two major depressive disorder subtypes with contrasting abnormal patterns of abnormality

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objective to identify MDD subtypes based on subject-level functional connectivity abnormalities using a tolerance interval-based approach.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: In this study, we sought to identify potential MDD subtypes from subjectlevel abnormalities in functional connectivity, leveraging a large multi-site dataset... Subject-level extreme functional connections... were used to identify biological subtypes of MDD.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses an existing dataset (REST-meta-MDD) and cites the original publications for eligibility criteria. It reports the final sample size (1104 HCs) and mentions exclusion criteria (implied via citation and 'matched' description). Image quality is addressed via citation to the preprocessing protocol and reporting of Mean FD.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: The imaging datasets for MDD used in this study were sourced from the REST-meta-MDD consortium (http://rfmri.org/RESTmeta-MDD) [31, 32]... comprising... 1104 HCs... Further demographic, clinical and imaging details are available in previous publications [31, 32].
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Materials and Methods, Imaging dataset and preprocessing

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The study addresses site effects using ComBat harmonization. However, it does not explicitly state that biological covariates like age and sex were regressed out or modeled within the tolerance interval construction for the reference cohort, which is a standard component of normative modeling. The tolerance intervals appear to be calculated on the harmonized data without further adjustment for age/sex trends.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Given the multi-site nature of the data collection... we applied the Combat method to harmonize the functional connections across these sites... we used the 'tolerance' package in R... to estimate nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals for each functional connection in HCs.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Materials and Methods, Functional connectivity features and harmonization; Identifying extreme functional connections in MDD
